_about: Batches added to the sweep view (tools/sweep_analysis.py, viewer/sweep.html) after the one-knob sweep b9-b21 closed. Same shape as plans/hyperparam-sweep.json's `batches`; the reducer reads that file first, then this one. Each batch's reference is viewer/references.json's entry for it. Every batch is binned on its own horizon (the max step over its arms), so a 100M or 200M batch sits here as it is.

batches.expected_optimum: unknown; the user's question was whether a per-step cost changes what the policy learns to do about long games
batches.notes: The first batch of the 26-value observation era (obs26-20260907), on the horizon-anneal config of b24 (gamma 0.99 -> 0.999 and lambda 0.95 -> 0.999 over the first half, huber, T 256, minibatch 512) at 50M, 4 seeds a cell. The reference in references.json is b24's own cell -- 200M and the 30-value era, so a loose one -- and pen0 is the batch's own control.

cells.prediction: the control: the b24 config at 50M under the 26-value observation
large enough to be felt against the b2 reward preset's per-step terms; the cell to read

batches.expected_optimum: unknown; the question was whether the observation's missing piece is the recent path -- hist4 was the cell to read
batches.notes: The pen01 base of b26 (step penalty 0.01, the 26-value observation, the b24 horizon anneal) at 100M and 8 seeds a cell; SNEK_OBS_HISTORY=N appends two bits per past move (plans/obs-history.md). Every cell also carries SNEK_STEP_PENALTY=0.01, left off the cell env here so the depth is the one numeric key the axis sorts on. The reference in references.json is b26's pen01 cell -- 50M and 4 seeds, so a loose one; hist0 is the like-for-like control. hist0 and hist4 ran first (laptop + desktop), hist8 followed on the desktop.
